on_screen_text.text: Republican Senator crashes out over banning congressional stock trading: “Anybody want to be poor? I don’t”
SENATE HOMELAND SECURITY COMMITTEE HOLDS A BUSINESS MEETING ON PENDING LEGISLATION

BUT SOMEHOW IT'S I MADE MONEY. I DON'T KNOW HOW HOW MANY OF YOU MAKE MONEY? ANYBODY WANT TO BE POOR? I DON'T. SO THIS IDEA THAT WE'RE GOING TO ATTACK PEOPLE BECAUSE THEY MAKE MONEY IS WRONG. IS ABSOLUTELY WRONG. WE SHOULD CHERISH ALL OF OUR DIFFERENT BACKGROUNDS. EVERY ONE OF US HAS A DIFFERENT BACKGROUND, I'VE GOT A BUSINESS BACKGROUND, BUT WHAT I WAS JUST ACCUSED OF IS MAKING MONEY. AND SOMEHOW I CAN'T BE FAIR AND DO THINGS THE RIGHT WAY. SO I THINK IT'S DISGUSTING WHAT THIS WHAT IS GOING ON HERE.

spoken_summary: Senator Rick Scott defends having made money, stating that it's 'suspect' only because he was successful. He asks rhetorically, 'Anybody want to be poor? I don't.' He argues that attacking people for making money is 'absolutely wrong' and that his business background shouldn't imply he can't be fair. He concludes by calling the situation 'disgusting'.
audio_music: The audio consists entirely of Rick Scott's spoken dialogue during the hearing. There is no music or other sound.
editing_pacing: The video is a single, static talking-head shot of Rick Scott speaking. The pacing is determined by his speech, with text overlays added for emphasis.
central_claim: Republican Senator Rick Scott is portrayed as out-of-touch and angrily defensive of his wealth during a discussion about banning congressional stock trading.
intended_effect: To make the viewer perceive Rick Scott, and by extension Republicans, as prioritizing personal wealth over ethical governance.
